A 88-year-old female patient comes for a routine primary care visit, accompanied by family members
who report she experienced a stroke 5 months ago and is currently receiving physical therapy. Her vital
signs show: temperature 98.5°F (36.8°C), blood pressure 105/68 mmHg, pulse 93/min, and
respirations 14/min. The neurological examination reveals normal alertness, orientation, and speech,
with preserved bilateral strength and sensation. However, she demonstrates balance difficulties and
tends to fall toward her right side. Which additional neurological finding would most likely be present in
this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Truncal ataxia (B) Nystagmus (C) Hemispatial neglect (D) Intention
tremor (E) Hypotonia (F) Dysdiadochokinesia (G) Gait ataxia (H) Resting tremor (I) Hemineglect (J)
Dysarthria
 A. Resting tremor
B. Gait ataxia
C. Nystagmus
D. Hypotonia
E. Hemineglect
F. Intention tremor

G. Truncal ataxia
H. Dysarthria
I. Dysdiadochokinesia
J. Hemispatial neglect
